text:
morgan: saw a bump in OOMs after r12 roll, mostly on large-chat workloads (history ~10k tokens). stack shows allocator failing to reserve workspace for the new CUDA kernel pathway.
li: can you paste the logs? curious if it's prefilling KV into workspace or decode buffers eating it.
morgan: attaching snip from node logs — allocator tries to grab 1.2GB slab, fails, then retries and OOMs. small note: kernel chooser picked 'fused-attn-v2' for sequences >4096.

morgan: ```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] alloc: want=1260234240, avail=1073741824, slab=1, reason=workspace_kernel
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] kv: prefill=880MB, decode_buf=420MB, reserved_prefill_cap=1.0
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] gpu_oom: could not satisfy allocate(1260234240)
```
sara: that kv:prefill number looks high. which config is that from? default per-request cap is 1.0? we had switched to auto-prefill heuristics last week.

morgan: yeah — auto-prefill decided to fully prefill contexts > 50 tokens because of improved decode latency in tests. but when combined with fused-attn-v2 workspace (~1GB) it's pushing nodes over.

li: two levers: 1) kernel routing fallback to a low-memory kernel when workspace+prefill > threshold, or 2) enforce a decode-window cap / per-request kv prefill cap. both are fast to change.
david: +3 on kernel fallback. we can't silently degrade accuracy. but fallback to a non-fused kernel for high-history requests should keep latency within SLO.

morgan: perf tradeoffs: fused kernel saves 15-25% latency but needs +40% workspace. for steady tail we should prefer failing to prefill than OOMing. proposing changes:
- default per-request kv_prefill_cap = 0.6 (was 1.0)
- introduce decode_window_cap = 2048 tokens for streaming decode (break long histories into halo windows)
- kernel_fallback: if (workspace_est + kv_est) > 0.8 * gpu_free, route to low-memory kernel

sara: can we do a canary: change prefilling cap on one pool and enable kernel_fallback only in canary? prefer minimal global churn.

li: wrote a quick patch to compute workspace_est. pseudo-config:

```
serve.runtime.prefill_cap_per_request = 0.6
serve.runtime.decode_window_cap = 2048
serve.runtime.kernel_fallback_threshold = 0.8
```

li: also added buffer-reuse hint: reuse decode buffer across micro-batches when batch size small. should recover ~200MB on p3.xlarge.

morgan: nice. what's the plan to measure regression risk? we need token-level latency + perf counters before/after and kv hit/miss distribution.

david: ops-bot can run comparison job on canary group 17 for 2 hours and produce:
- 95/99 latency
- OOM counts
- avg kv_prefill per request
- kernel choice distribution

ops-bot: scheduling perf-compare job: canary=pool-17, baseline=pool-12, duration=2h. I will upload CSV to /perf/runs/1876543210.

sara: one more thought on fragmentation — frequent small alloc/free from KV slab causes fragmentation so even when free bytes > need, contiguous slab not available. we should try two things:
- round allocations to slab-size buckets (e.g., 16MB granularity)
- prefer reusing freed buffers from LRU freelist before asking allocator

li: implemented bucketed-slab allocator locally. microbench shows 18% less external fragmentation on synthetic KV churn. no functional change but reduces worst-case single allocation size by coalescing.

morgan: ok action items:
1) li to push prefill_cap + kernel_fallback + buffer_reuse to canary (pool-17) — ETA 2h
2) ops-bot to run perf-compare, upload CSV — ETA 2h after deploy
3) sara to validate model quality regressions on sampled prompts (we don't want windowing to drop context quality) — ETA 3h
4) david to prepare rollback plan if OOMs persist (pin old runtime)

li: starting rollout to canary now. will ping on results.

morgan: thanks. if canary looks good, let's roll to batch 25% then 100% over 6h.

sara: :thumbsup: also add alert to track kernel_fallback rate > 5% — that flags potential perf hit.

li: noted, adding monitoring for kernel_fallback_pct, avg_prefill_bytes, fragmentation_events.

morgan: closing loop later with perf CSV. thanks all.
